items.title: Negaunee council eyes zoning limits to confine data centers to mining and industrial zones
items.dek: The Negaunee City Council scheduled a public hearing for its Aug. 13 meeting on a new ordinance that would restrict data centers to specific zones and impose strict noise, pollution and height rules. Council members have said the language aims to give the city control and potentially deter projects.
items.source: Negaunee City Council or Planning Commission agenda
items.findings: Ordinance would limit data centers to mining and industrial zones per the July 20 Mining Journal report | Requires any air pollution, dust, smoke, glare, exhaust, noise, heat, vibration or humidity to be imperceptible at or beyond the property line | Sets maximum building heights and other specifications | City Council voted 7-0 on first reading in July and scheduled the hearing | Councilperson Jon Becker said he hopes the rules are so restrictive that projects go elsewhere | Councilperson Amanda Ghanavati said she hopes it makes data centers nearly impossible here
items.perspective: The Negaunee Planning Commission drafted and recommended the ordinance last month. Michigan law bars exclusionary zoning that would fully prohibit data centers. The Aug. 13 public hearing is the next step before a potential second reading and vote.
items.judge_note: Concrete new development: Negaunee scheduled a public hearing on Aug. 13 for a specific zoning ordinance restricting data centers.
